title: Projective iteration of the universal stable pointed curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $g\geq2$ and $n\geq0$ integers, and $T_0$ a finite-type H-projective $k$-scheme. Let $a_0:T_0\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ specify a stable unpointed genus-$g$ family. Use the stable ordered pointed moduli groupoids of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For $r\geq0$, let $F_r:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r+1}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r}$ forget the last marking and stabilize, with the contraction and stabilization convention of [lem-sfb-knudsen-pointed-forgetful-universal-curve].

There exist schemes $T_r$ and maps $a_r:T_r\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r}$ for $0\leq r\leq n$, starting from the specified $T_0,a_0$, and maps $q_r:T_{r+1}\to T_r$ for $r<n$, such that every square with horizontal maps $a_{r+1},a_r$ and vertical maps $q_r,F_r$ is 2-cartesian. If $(X_r\to T_r,s_{1,r},\ldots,s_{r,r})$ is the family specified by $a_r$, then $T_{r+1}=X_r$ and $q_r$ is its structural morphism; the family specified by $a_{r+1}$ is the stabilized family obtained by appending the tautological extra section on $X_r\times_{T_r}X_r$. Each $T_r$ is finite type and H-projective over $k$. Each $q_r$ is H-projective, flat and finitely presented, as well as projective in the projective-bundle convention. For any $k$-scheme $B$ and map $b:B\to T_r$, the pullback of the family specified by $a_r$ is a stable ordered $r$-pointed genus-$g$ family, with bundle projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, nodal geometric fibres, disjoint smooth sections and the component stability inequalities.

Field, scheme, finite type, H-projectivity, bundle projectivity, stable pointed curves, smoothness, flatness and finite presentation use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The 2-cartesian terminology and pullbacks have the groupoid meaning in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

proof.text: Induct on the length $r$ of the whole tower. Retain all $T_j,a_j$ for $0\leq j\leq r$ and $q_j$ for $j<r$, every earlier 2-cartesian square, the finite-type and H-projective structure morphisms of every $T_j$, and the H-projectivity, bundle projectivity, flatness and finite presentation of every $q_j$. Each $a_j$ must specify a stable ordered $j$-pointed genus-$g$ family. At $r=0$ take the specified $T_0,a_0$; there are no transition morphisms or squares to check. A map to the moduli groupoid means an actual family, so write the family at the last stage as $X_r\to T_r$ with its labelled sections.

source.place: Agent induction from the universal-curve identification in Section 2; base case and the moduli-groupoid convention.

proof.text: Assume the invariant at $r<n$. Apply the Knudsen universal-curve theorem to $(X_r/T_r,s_{1,r},\ldots,s_{r,r})$, with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Choose its representing scheme itself as $T_{r+1}=X_r$ and put $q_r:X_r\to T_r$ equal to the structural map. The universal extra point is the section $x\mapsto(x,x)$ of $X_r\times_{T_r}X_r\to X_r$ (projection to the base factor); the old sections are $x\mapsto(s_{i,r}(q_r(x)),x)$ when the second factor is the base. The theorem stabilizes this family with its extra section, giving $a_{r+1}$ and the comparison $F_r a_{r+1}\cong a_r q_r$. To check the square, evaluate on a $k$-scheme $B$. Its 2-fibre product has objects $(b,Y,\phi)$: a map $b:B\to T_r$, a stable $(r+1)$-pointed family $Y/B$, and an ordered-family isomorphism $\phi:F_r(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}b^*a_r$. The cited theorem identifies this groupoid naturally with maps $B\to X_r$ over $T_r$, by its mutually inverse contraction and stabilization. This is precisely the defining 2-cartesian property, with automorphisms and all old labels retained. It also gives bundle projectivity, flatness and finite presentation of $q_r$. Its stabilization includes collisions with old markings and nodes, so no distinctness condition is imposed on the tautological point.

source.place: Section 2, especially Corollary 2.6; the existing universal-curve theorem supplies representation, stabilization, and its arbitrary-base naturality.

proof.text: By the inductive H-projectivity and its definition choose a closed immersion $T_r\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$. Apply the projective-ample-invertible lemma with $A=k$ and this immersion: its pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ is an ample invertible sheaf on $T_r$. The bundle-to-H-projective lemma therefore applies to the bundle-projective $q_r$ from step 2 and makes $q_r$ H-projective. Compose $q_r$ with the H-projective structure map of $T_r$ using H-projective composition. Thus $T_{r+1}$ is H-projective over $k$. The ample sheaf is obtained anew on each $T_r$; bundle projectivity alone has not been used as an unconditional H-projectivity assertion.

source.place: Tags 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), clause (1), and 01WE (lemma-H-projective-composition); ample sheaf from Properties Tag 01PU and projective-space twisting sheaves as in the cited ample lemma.

proof.text: The finite presentation of $q_r$ includes quasi-compactness. In its affine presentations $R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/(f_1,\ldots,f_e)$ the images of the finitely many variables generate the algebra; thus it is locally of finite type. With quasi-compactness, this is finite type by definition. Apply clause (1) of the finite-type composition lemma with $f=q_r:T_{r+1}\to T_r$ and $h:T_r\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is finite type by the inductive invariant. Their composite is the specified $k$-structure map of $T_{r+1}$, so $T_{r+1}$ is finite type over $k$. Steps 2--4 establish the invariant at $r+1$ while retaining the earlier tower. Finite induction constructs the required tower through $n$; for $n=0$ no $q_r$ or square is required.

source.place: Definition Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation), Definition Tag 01T0 (definition-finite-type), and Tag 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); finite presentation implies finite type by the displayed affine presentation.

proof.text: For any $0\le r\le n$, the constructed $a_r$ specifies a stable ordered $r$-pointed genus-$g$ family. Apply the arbitrary-base-change clause of the Knudsen theorem to any $k$-scheme $B$ and $b:B\to T_r$. The result is again a stable ordered $r$-pointed genus-$g$ family in the same convention. Unpacking the stable-family definition gives bundle projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, nodal geometric fibres, disjoint smooth sections and the component stability inequalities requested. The moduli convention retains the ordered labels and the genus. No finite-type, reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $B$ is introduced.

source.place: Section 2, arbitrary-base-change naturality and stability; the stable-family and ordered moduli definitions spell out all the requested clauses.
